subject: Snapshot & retention questionnaire — logs, backups, prompts

Subject: Questions on log/snapshot/prompt retention for SOC/SIG

Hi Rachel,

We are finalizing our SIG profile and need a short, factual response about Redwood's default data retention behavior for the following items: request logs (metadata), full request bodies/prompts, automated backups/snapshots, and any media artifacts. Specific asks:
- Default retention period for request logs (and whether metadata vs body are treated differently).
- Are backup snapshots immutable? If so, for how long?
- Is prompt/utterance text persisted in backups or retained longer than live logs?
- Where can we find supporting evidence (policy docs, SOC 2 control mapping, or screenshots) to attach to our questionnaire?

We appreciate concise, attributable answers (we'll quote them in the SIG). If you need to loop in your privacy or ops folks that's fine — we can wait 48–72 hours for a response.

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on log/snapshot/prompt retention for SOC/SIG

Rachel — quick facts (authoritative; ops verified). I'll draft a short statement you can send: 

1) Request logs (metadata): default retention 30 days. Metadata includes request time, model, token counts, response latency.
2) Request bodies / prompts (full text): persisted for 14 days by default for debugging and quality purposes, then deleted. Customers can opt into longer retention for analytics or fine-tuning via account settings and a contract addendum.
3) Backups / snapshots: encrypted snapshots of system state and persistent storage are retained for 13 months (395 days). Snapshots are write-once in object storage (immutable snapshots) for an initial 30-day immutability window, after which lifecycle rules may transition or expire them per the 13-month policy.
4) Prompts in backups: snapshot backups may include persisted data from the live system at snapshot time; if prompts are present in persisted storage at snapshot time they will be included. Because prompt bodies are deleted from live storage after 14 days by default, they are only captured in backups if the snapshot window overlaps with the retention window.
5) KV caches / ephemeral state: not persisted to durable backups; short-lived, TTL <= 1 hour by default.

Evidence and artifacts I will attach: retention matrix (PDF), snapshots of the admin console retention config, and the SOC 2 control mapping excerpt that maps these behaviors to CC6/CC7 controls.

Marissa, confirming the export names and whether we can include a sanitized S3 listing screenshot for the snapshot retention evidence.

-Karthik
Director, Privacy & Compliance

Hi Elena — thanks for your patience. Below are concise, quotable answers you can use in the SIG/CAIQ. Attached is a zip with supporting artifacts (retention matrix, redacted S3 index, admin console screenshots) and a short signed statement we can provide if you need one.

- Request logs (metadata): Default retention = 30 days. Metadata includes timestamps, model id, latency and token counts; it is stored for operational troubleshooting and telemetry only.
- Request bodies / prompts (full text): Default retention = 14 days. Prompt bodies are purged after 14 days unless the customer explicitly enables extended retention via account settings and contract.
- Backups / snapshots: Retained for 13 months (395 days). Snapshots are write-once (immutable) for the first 30 days; after 30 days lifecycle rules may transition or expire objects in accordance with the 13-month policy. Snapshots are encrypted at rest.
- Prompts in backups: Prompts are included in backups only if present on disk at snapshot time. Because prompts are deleted from live storage after 14 days by default, they are generally not present in snapshots taken outside that window.
- Ephemeral caches: KV caches and in-memory caches are not persisted to durable backups and have default TTL <= 1 hour.

If you would like a signed statement for your records I have attached 'signed-statement-mednexa.pdf' (signed by our Head of Security). Let me know if you need any further redactions or a specific control mapping into the SIG/CAIQ matrix and we'll provide it.

Next step: please confirm whether the above can be quoted in your submission and if you want the signed statement.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
